{{Quote|They are ancient Sith bred into hulking warriors.|[[Talos Drellik]]|<ref name="TOR:FPWK">{{TORcite|exp=kotfe|type=general|Fighting Power With Knowledge|Yavin 4}}</ref>}}
The '''Massassi''' were a [[Subspecies/Legends|subspecies]] of the [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith species]] who were [[Slavery/Legends|enslaved]] by [[Exiles|exiled]] [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] on [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]]. Massassi were fearsome, loyal, and formidable warriors, and as such comprised the warrior class in the Sith caste system. They lived solely to serve their Sith masters, but when on their own, dedicated themselves only to whatever life they chose.

==Biology and appearance==
{{Quote|They really are amazingly malleable, the Massassi.|[[Ajunta Pall]]|<ref name="JvS:TEGttF">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref>}}
[[File:Massassi_at_the_funeral_of_Marka_Ragnos.jpg|thumb|left|100px|Massassi warriors]]
Like the rest of the [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith]],<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> the Massassi subspecies<ref name="KotORCG" /><ref name="JvS:TEGttF" /> were native to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]], within the isolated [[Stygian Caldera]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. They, like the few other creatures that inhabited Korriban, derived sustenance directly from the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]],<ref name="TEA" /> in part of a natural symbiotic relationship where Sith&mdash;like the Massassi&mdash;fed on the dark side, and empowered it in turn.<ref name="TotJC">''[[Tales of the Jedi Companion]]''</ref> Thus the entire Sith race, including the Massassi,<ref name="KotORCG" /> had such a high rate of [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitivity]]<ref name="JATM">''[[Jedi Academy Training Manual]]''</ref> that they were considered a naturally Force-sensitive species.<ref name="JvS:TEGttF" />

Phenotypically, Massassi were quite similar to the rest of the Sith species. Common to all Sith, Massassi skin was red,<ref name="GAotS" /><ref name="FotSE" /> ranging from florid<ref name="LTotSPr">''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Precipice]]''</ref> crimsons<ref name="KotORCG" /><ref name="JvS:TEGttF" /> to lighter pinks.<ref name="GAotS" /><ref name="FotSE" /> Massassi had fierce, predatory profiles,<ref name="JvS:TEGttF" /> and sharp<ref name="KotORCG" /> bone spurs protruding over their bodies in various locations<ref name="Crosscurrent">''[[Crosscurrent]]''</ref>&mdash;especially the elbows.<ref name="GAotS" /><ref name="FotSE" /> Other facial features included a pair of tendrils that hung from their cheekbones,<ref name="GAotS" /><ref name="FotSE" /> and cartilaginous<ref name="Crosscurrent" /> eyebrow stalks that covered their eyes.<ref name="LTotSPa">''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Paragon]]''</ref> They also had simian mouths, small noses<ref name="GAotS" /><ref name="FotSE" /> and ears,<ref name="Crosscurrent" /> and a slightly receding chin. Like other Sith, Massassi had three digits on each of their hands and feet.<ref name="GAotS" /><ref name="FotSE" />

Exclusive to their subspecies however, Massassi possessed large<ref name="GAotS" /><ref name="FotSE" /> glowing [[Color/Legends|yellow]] [[Eye/Legends|eyes]].<ref name="KotORCG" /><ref name="JvS:TEGttF" /> Unlike mainline Sith, the eyes of Massassi did not display details such as pupils or whites of any sort&mdash;instead the yellow seemed to cover the whole of each eye. Massassi were also taller,<ref name="GAotS" /><ref name="FotSE" /> larger, and more hulking humanoids than the species they hailed from,<ref name="KotORCG" /> reaching between two and three [[Meter/Legends|meters]] in height,<ref name="LTotSPr" /> and an average weight of ninety-five [[Kilogram/Legends|kilograms]].<ref name="KotORCG" /> Massassi senses were very acute compared to those of [[Human/Legends|Humans]]&mdash;particularly their hearing.<ref name="Crosscurrent" /> Massassi also had an extremely tough skin; powerful cauterizing agents such as [[cyanogen silicate]] were needed to provide Massassi with medical assistance. Nothing weaker was capable of corroding their resistant hides.<ref name="LTotSPr" />

[[File:Massassi_architects.png|thumb|right|200px|Massassi architects]]
Relative to other species, Massassi were quite short lived. The typical Massassi childhood lasted ten standard years, with the next three standard years constituting young adulthood. Massassi adulthood typically began at around fourteen standard years of age. Middle age started after twenty-five standard years of life, and old age after thirty-five years. Any Massassi over the age of fifty standard years were considered venerable.<ref name="KotORCG" />

The Massassi under the command of [[Naga Sadow/Legends|Naga Sadow]] that relocated to [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]] after the Great Hyperspace War underwent [[Sith alchemy/Legends|alchemical]] alterations under the supervision of Sadow. These individuals and their descendants became more hunched and monstrous than the original Massassi species, and were gradually considered more like savage brutes than the warriors they once were. At this point, they became large creatures with sharp claws and grotesque fin-like growths on their head and back.<ref name="Essential Guide to Alien Species" />

==Society and culture==
{{Quote|They failed to learn the lesson of humility. The grander their works, the more they ached for the power that still seemed so far out of reach. They gathered these stones for the Sith in a vain effort to touch the face of their god. And they pursued the dark power of the Sith in a vain effort to become like gods themselves.|[[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker's]] view on the species after reading the [[Books of Massassi]]|<ref name="BtSt">''[[Before the Storm]]''</ref>}}
[[File:RMQ-TempleBlueleafCluster.jpg|thumb|left|350px|The Massassi used hieroglyphs (left) in their temples.]]
The Massassi were fearsome, ruthless, and efficient soldiers.<ref name="KotORCG" /> They made use of [[Massassi (alphabet)|Massassi hieroglyphs]] which were written on their artifacts as well as structures.<ref name="U:TYV">''[[Star Wars: Underworld: The Yavin Vassilika]]''</ref> During the reign of Exar Kun, the race had largely devolved into mindless brutes that followed the commands of their master. There were notable elements within their culture, however, such as the presence of priests and elders.<ref name="Essential Guide to Alien Species" />

The Massassi warriors who had accompanied Naga Sadow in exile had come to regard the [[Gas giant/Legends|gas giant]] [[Yavin Prime/Legends|Yavin Prime]] as a fearsome but fascinating deity they called [[Yavin (deity)|Yavin]]. The warriors felt humbled by their new god's all-dominating presence. As they could not withstand their own hubris, the Massassi made a vain attempt to achieve godly status by assembling temples and monuments for their worldly masters.<ref name="BtSt" />

They were not only fearsome, but both loyal and formidable warriors that were dedicated to their Sith masters. In addition to the focus on war and fighting, the Massassi were also loyal and organized.<ref name="KotORCG" /> They were bred to blindly follow orders and to live for the glory of battle.<ref name="DSS">''[[The Dark Side Sourcebook]]''</ref> Even though they were not extremely intelligent, they could be trained well enough to carry out complex battle plans and maintain their equipment, starships, and weaponry. The Massassi also used alchemically hardened armor and a more primitive version of the [[Sith lanvarok]] which could also be used as a battle axe; this variant was known as the [[Massassi lanvarok]].<ref name="KotORCG" />

In battle, the Massassi typically had a keeper who watched over them as these nasty lumbering bipeds were normally prized by the Sith as instruments of terror on the battlefield. As such, they were known as pliant and obedient warriors but answered more to force rather than words.<ref name="LTotSPr" />

==History==
{{Quote|Eventually all of the Sith&hellip;especially their Massassi warriors&hellip;lived only to serve their new masters.|[[Ajunta Pall]]|<ref name="JvS:TEGttF" />}}
[[File:Massassi-JATM.jpg|thumb|right|180px|A Kissai priest (left) and a Massassi warrior (right), both of Sith blood]]
The Massassi were a subspecies of the Sith,<ref name="KotORCG" /> a sentient species native to the planet Korriban that had formed a civilization in [[100,000 BBY/Legends|100,000 BBY]].<ref name="JvS:TEGttF" /> The [[Kissai]] were the Sith's priest caste, while the second-order [[Zuguruk]] were the engineers, whilst the Massassi below them were the warriors and the [[Grotthu]] being the lowliest caste comprising enslaved beings of a variety of species.<ref name="BOS">''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]''</ref> The Kissai and the Massassi<ref name="KotORCG" /> resettled on the [[Sith Empire (Pre-Republic)|Sith Empire's]] capital world of [[Ziost/Legends|Ziost]] around [[27,700 BBY]].<ref name="JvS:TEGttF" />

Around [[6900 BBY]], [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] who were [[Exiles|exiled]] from the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] after their [[Battle of Corbos|defeat]] in the [[Hundred-Year Darkness/Legends|Hundred-Year Darkness]] [[Discovery of Korriban|discovered]] Korriban and established themselves as "divine" rulers over the Sith, becoming the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lords of the Sith]] ruling a new [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]].<ref name="JvS:TEGttF" /> Over the generations, the original Sith Purebloods interbred with the Human Dark Jedi. The Dark Lords found the Massassi useful as tools of power, and much of the Sith Empire's military was composed of Massassi warriors.<ref name="KotORCG" />

In [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]],<ref name="TEC" /> during the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]], the Massassi proved to be formidable and savage warriors that fought against the Galactic Republic on behalf of the Dark Lord of the Sith [[Naga Sadow/Legends|Naga Sadow]].<ref name="fall3">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire 3|''Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire'' 3]]</ref> Some Massassi were aboard the ''[[Omen]]'' and were stranded on the planet [[Kesh/Legends|Kesh]].<ref name="LTotSPr" /> Despite the fury of the Massassi, the Sith forces were defeated and forced to return to Sith space, where Republic forces [[Second battle of Korriban|pursued and attacked]] the [[Sith invasion fleet]]. In order to survive, Sadow commanded his loyal Massassi to give their lives and delay the Republic so he could escape. This resulted in the Massassi assassinating their Sith Lords on board Sadow's fleet and engaging the Republic, thus giving their master the chance to flee the battlefield.<ref name="fall5" />

===Yavin 4===
{{Quote|The beings who dwell here are called Massassi&hellip;primitive&hellip;brutal&hellip;the descendants of the Ancient Sith.|[[Freedon Nadd]]|audio=FreedonNaddMassassi-DLOTS.flac|<ref name="Tales of the Jedi: Dark Lords of the Sith (audio)">[[Tales of the Jedi: Dark Lords of the Sith (audio drama)|''Tales of the Jedi: Dark Lords of the Sith'' audio drama]]</ref>}}
[[File:TempleofYavin4-AoRCR.png|thumb|left|350px|The Massassi built temples on Yavin 4]]
Sadow fled to the jungle moon of [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]] along with a contingent of Massassi followers to escape the pursuing Galactic Republic military forces.<ref name="fall5" /> There, Sadow subjected his Massassi warriors to [[Sith alchemy/Legends|Sith alchemy]], which resulted in them becoming [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] wielding savages. Despite these abuses, the Massassi built temples to honor<ref name="darklords4" /> their Lord.<ref name="golden4">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith 4|''Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith'' 4]]</ref> Eventually the Massassi on the moon devolved into a primitive hunter-warrior society.<ref name="darklords4" /> At some point during the construction of the Massassi Temples, they created the [[Yavin Vassilika]] that contained a key to one of the more strategically important temples.<ref name="U:TYV" />

In [[3997 BBY]],<ref name="TEC" /> [[Exar Kun/Legends|Exar Kun]] elevated himself to the status of a god and enslaved the Massassi members on Yavin IV. He then forced them to construct a great complex of temples that were used in arcane [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] ceremonies and rites. He also experimented on his slaves<ref name="darklords5">[[Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith 5|''Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith'' 5]]</ref> and created the [[Golden Globe]] that trapped the children of the Massassi and allowed him to drain their energies for his own purposes.<ref name="TEC" /> The Massassi served Exar Kun when he [[Duel in the Iron Citadel (Exar Kun)|snuck into the Iron Citadel]]<ref name="darklords6">[[Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith 6|''Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith'' 6]]</ref> and during the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]].<ref name="sithwar5">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War 5|''Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War'' 5]]</ref> During the [[Battle of Yavin 4 (Great Sith War)|Battle of Yavin 4]] at the end of the Great Sith War<ref name="sithwar6">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War 6|''Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War'' 6]]</ref> in [[3996 BBY]],<ref name="TEC" /> [[Exar Kun/Legends|Exar Kun]] sapped the life out most of the Massassi on [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]] so that he could free his soul from his body in order to survive the [[Wall of light]] created by the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]].<ref name="sithwar6" /> Some of the Massassi survived Kun's ritual, one example was [[Kalgrath]].<ref name="Essential Guide to Alien Species" /> In addition, there were Massassi living on other worlds. For example, there was at least [[Unidentified half breed Massassi|one Massassi]] living on Korriban in [[3993 BBY]],<ref name="shadows">{{Tales|23|Shadows and Light}}</ref> and reports of isolated villages of both [[Kissai]] and Massassi on Korriban<ref name="KotORCG" /> and [[Tund/Legends|Tund]].<ref name="Web Enhancement">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/KOTORweben5|text=KOTOR Campaign Guide Web Enhancement 5: Karnak Tetsu, Sorcerer of Tund}}</ref>

Though nearly annihilated, some Massassi had previously been taken off world which meant that the species was not largely extinct at the time. Some of its members, however, quickly went into the service of the new [[Darth Revan's Sith Empire|Sith Empire]] that had formed during the [[Jedi Civil War]]. Some also remained neutral as they were resentful of the treatment done to their race by the Sith. These Massassi either decided to continue a life where they could live in peace while others stayed in the fringes of society and sought revenge against the Sith.<ref name="KotORCG" />

[[File:Ovair_Gynt_vs_Massassi.jpg|thumb|right|350px|Master Ovair and Padawan Gynt battle mutated Massassi warriors on Yavin 4.]]
In the years before the [[Great Galactic War]], the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|True Sith]] hiding in the shadows of the galaxy began dispatching their infiltrated agents in the Jedi Order such as [[Barel Ovair]] to remove any threats posed by ancient dark side spirits such as that of Naga Sadow. To that end, he travelled with his [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Eison Gynt]] to Yavin 4 to study the temple there though Gynt was unaware of his master's true allegiance. Upon arriving, they were attacked by the native Massassi who had survived the events caused by Exar Kun, and overwhelmed Ovair and Gynt to the point that they fled to Sadow's tomb. From the encounter, only Master Ovair emerged and returned to the [[Jedi Council/Legends|Jedi Council]]. Seven years later, Gynt emerged wearing Massassi warrior robes and had been possessed by the dark side spirit of Naga Sadow from the tomb. Gynt attacked master Ovair in broad daylight with all the Republic watching, and although a formidable opponent with Sadow's powers, Ovair was able to defeat the possessed Gynt.<ref name="Time7">{{TORweb|url=holonet/galactic-history|text=Timeline 7: Peace for the Republic?|int=Timeline 7: Peace for the Republic?}}</ref>

Around [[400 BBY/Legends|four hundred years]] before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], the [[Kushiban]] [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Ikrit]] discovered the Golden Globe in the ruined [[Palace of the Woolamander]] and since he was unable to free the Massassi from the swirling golden sand within the globe, placed himself in hibernation for centuries, until the right being or beings arrived. Many scholars believed that the species had gone extinct by the time of the [[Rise of the Empire era|rise of the Empire]] though it was possible that some managed to survive on forgotten Sith worlds or had devolved into predatory savages on distant worlds.<ref name="DSS" /> Finally, in [[22 ABY/Legends|22 ABY]], [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] trainees [[Anakin Solo]] and [[Tahiri Veila]] freed the trapped spirits from the swirling golden sand of the globe, and in the process befriended the mysterious Ikrit. By this point, the Massassi were largely extinct with many archaeologists as well as linguists attempting to learn more about the mysterious race. It was known that the last known member of the species known as Kalgrath departed to Ziost, one of the former strongholds of the Sith Empire but little else was known about his fate.<ref name="Essential Guide to Alien Species" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:MassassiWarrior.jpg|thumb|right|180px|Dario Carrasco, Jr.'s sketch of a Massassi warrior]]
The earliest mentions of the name in comics by [[Archie Goodwin]] spell it as "Massasi,"<ref name="SW25">[[Star Wars (1977) 25|''Star Wars'' (1977) 25]]</ref><ref name="SW26">[[Star Wars (1977) 26|''Star Wars'' (1977) 26]]</ref><ref name="SW27">[[Star Wars (1977) 27|''Star Wars'' (1977) 27]]</ref> until the [[Star Wars Weekly]] story ''[[The Day after the Death Star!]]'' spelt it the current way.

The rebel base exterior and its environs on Yavin 4 in [[George Lucas]]' [[1977]] film [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']] are shots of the ruined [[Wikipedia:Maya civilization|Mayan]] city of [[Tikal]] in [[Wikipedia:Guatemala|Guatemala]].<ref name="BTM">''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]''</ref> The extant temples were defined as the built legacy of the Massassi civilization [[in-universe]] by later [[Star Wars Legends|Expanded Universe]] sources and storytelling.

Inscriptions drawn by [[Ralph McQuarrie]], the lead concept artist for the ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[original trilogy]], in a piece showing rebels exploring a temple,<ref name="Illustrated">''[[The Illustrated Star Wars Universe]]''</ref> were established as Massassi writing in the article "[[The Written Word]]," written by [[John Hazlett]] and published on [[StarWars.com]]'s [[Hyperspace: The Official Star Wars Fan Club|Hyperspace]] feature in [[2010]].<ref name="Written">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/source/writtenword/index.html?page=1|text=The Written Word|int=The Written Word}}</ref>

In [[Kevin J. Anderson]]'s [[Dark Apprentice (novel)|''Dark Apprentice'']], [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] has a [[Dream/Legends|nightmare]] involving Massassi workers straining enormous stone blocks. In his dream they are grayish-green humanoids with smooth skin and "large lanternlike eyes"<ref name="DA">[[Dark Apprentice (novel)|''Dark Apprentice'']]</ref> rather than red-skinned humanoids with sharp features,<ref name="darklords4" /> which stands to reason as there is no evidence Luke had ever encountered an actual Massassi aside from [[Kalgrath]], who was green when Luke met him.<ref name="TNB">"[[The Night Beast]]"</ref>
